Mina — reviewed the customer's redlines and dug into the exhibits. High level: we can accept most of the edits but there are three items I want to surface before we send a consolidated counter:

1) SLA credits: their proposed credit matrix is broader than our standard playbook; recommend we cap credits to avoid creating a new precedent across renewals for this segment.
2) Data/export controls in Exhibit (they added some language around cross-border processing): we need to ensure compatibility with our standard data residency commitments and any subcontractor obligations. Recommend a narrow concession that preserves export controls language but references our KMS and subprocessors list.
3) Termination liability: the redline expands customer remedies for early termination tied to usage triggers. Suggest we keep liability capped at a short multiple of monthly charges for the committed term.

Playbook recommendation on exhibits: keep exhibits separate but add an exhibit-linking clause in the MSA that defines sequencing and precedence (this lets billing stay operationally separate while keeping a single point of contractual truth). That addresses Jamie's question while minimizing drafting churn.

I've produced a consolidated redline (Stellar_Renewal_MSA_Redline_v3.docx) and a short redline-summary.pdf that lists the three items and our recommended language. Also updated OrderForm_Stellar_v2.xlsx with a billing schedule reflecting +20% uplift and new effective date.

If we agree internally, I recommend we: 1) send the consolidated redline to the customer with the summary, 2) offer a single 30–45 minute alignment call to close the three open points, and 3) provide a targeted DocuSign packet once we have agreed language.

Approving to send to customer pending Mina's go-ahead.

—Lauren
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Jamie — thanks for your patience. Attached are the consolidated materials: Stellar_Renewal_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (consolidated MSA redline), OrderForm_Stellar_v2.xlsx (updated billing schedule reflecting +20% uplift), and redline-summary.pdf (short summary of the three open points).

Summary of the three items we highlighted and our recommended positions:
- SLA credits: Redwood will accept a limited credit structure tied to actual downtime for the committed services; we propose a monthly cap equal to 50% of the monthly committed fee and a max aggregate cap equal to three months' fees for the 18-month renewal period.
- Data/export language: we agreed to narrow export control language referencing Redwood's subprocessors and KMS controls; we will not accept broad obligations that require source-code escrow or unlimited export warranties.
- Termination/liability: liability remains capped to a multiple of monthly committed fees (equal to 6x monthly for the committed term) with carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct.

Next steps we propose:
1) Quick alignment call — propose Thu Aug 2 at 10:00am PT (I can send an invite).
2) If those three items are acceptable in principle, we'll send a DocuSign packet (link below) with the consolidated MSA and order form prepared for signature.
